seoTitle: How to Change Page URL in Elementor (Fix Slug)
metaDescription: Learn how to change a page URL or slug in WordPress when using Elementor, and fix issues if the page doesn't load correctly after the change.
intro: Many beginners assume Elementor controls the page URL, but the actual link or slug is managed through WordPress's own page settings. This guide clears up where to change it, how to keep menus and internal links working, and what to check if the page stops loading after an update.

steps.heading: Understand where the URL is controlled
steps.body: The page's URL or permalink is managed by WordPress itself, not by Elementor's page editor, even though Elementor controls the visual design.

steps.heading: Change the page URL/permalink
steps.body: From the WordPress page editor, edit the permalink field directly below the page title to update the slug.

steps.heading: Fix pages not loading after a URL change
steps.body: If the page doesn't load correctly after changing the slug, clear your cache and check that no plugin is still referencing the old URL.

steps.heading: Update menus and internal links
steps.body: After changing a URL, manually update any navigation menu items or internal links that pointed to the old slug so they don't break.

steps.heading: Follow SEO best practices for URLs
steps.body: Keep new URLs short, readable, and relevant to the page content, and consider setting up a redirect from the old URL if the page was already indexed.

faq.question: Does Elementor control the page URL?
faq.answer: No, the page URL or permalink is managed by WordPress's core page settings, not Elementor's design editor.

faq.question: Why does my page show an error after changing the slug?
faq.answer: This is usually due to cached references to the old URL or internal links/menus still pointing to the previous slug.

faq.question: Should I redirect the old URL after changing it?
faq.answer: Yes, if the page was already live and indexed, setting up a redirect from the old URL to the new one helps preserve SEO value and avoid broken links.

faq.question: Can changing a URL break my Elementor template?
faq.answer: The Elementor design itself isn't affected by a URL change, but any dynamic links referencing the old slug elsewhere on the site will need updating.
